fields.text: ISAF falls back to Los Canas
lines: ISAF falls back to Los Canas

fields.text:
The retreat has a name now, and the name is Los Canas.

ISAF's first offensive against Stonehenge has failed. The official chronology records that ISAF was pushed back to Los Canas and that its first attack on the battery failed on 14 September 2003. Allied columns are falling back along every road to the coast, covered by whatever aircraft can still fly. Supply depots that took months to fill are being burned in days so that the Erusean army cannot use them.

At Los Canas the allied command is digging in. Engineers are laying mines across the approaches, and the harbour is crowded with ships waiting to evacuate the wounded. The staff officers do not use the word "defeat" in their reports. They write about consolidation, about regrouping, and about time — the one thing the allies still have and Erusea, overstretched across a continent, does not.

fields.text: ISAF headquarters moves to North Point
lines: ISAF headquarters moves to North Point

fields.text:
The headquarters moved by night, in convoys of ships with their lights off.

ISAF has left the continent. Its command, its records and its surviving air wings are now based on North Point, the island nation beyond the reach of Stonehenge's guns. The official chronology records that ISAF established its headquarters in North Point on 16 September 2004.

From the island, the allied command is rebuilding: training new pilots on runways the railguns cannot touch, repairing ships in North Point's yards, and planning a return that the Erusean broadcasts insist will never come. On the continent, the occupied cities wait. Some of the people in them listen to North Point's radio station at night, with the volume turned low.

fields.text: ISAF lands on the Usean continent
lines: ISAF lands on the Usean continent

fields.text:
Before dawn, the first landing craft hit the beaches.

After a year of preparation on North Point, ISAF has returned to the Usean continent. The official chronology records that ISAF landed on 24 January 2005. Allied aircraft are flying cover from forward strips cut out of farmland. Behind the first waves come engineers, fuel bladders and the long tail of an army that intends to stay.

The Erusean command, which has spent a year holding a continent with an army built for a short war, now has to decide where to defend and what to give up. Along the occupied roads, people have started taking down the posters.

fields.text: Stonehenge is destroyed
lines: Stonehenge is destroyed

fields.text:
For the first time since the war began, allied aircraft are flying over the San Salvacion desert without dying.

ISAF has destroyed Stonehenge. The official chronology records that the battery was destroyed on 2 April 2005, with seven of its eight railguns knocked out. The strike crews who came back from the desert do not say much about it.

The weapon was built to protect Usea from Ulysses, under an international project that was meant to belong to everyone. It has ended as a ruin, after two years of being turned against the people it was built for. Allied commanders note that Erusea has lost its shield in the sky. The engineers who designed the battery are less ready to celebrate.

lines: The Mount Shezna radar

The radar station on Mount Shezna is gone.

The official chronology records that the Mount Shezna radar was destroyed on 10 October 2004, to cover ISAF's retreat from Saint Ark. With the radar silenced, the allied columns pulling back from Saint Ark had a chance to get clear. Nobody on the staff pretends it was anything but a retreat; everybody agrees it was a retreat that kept an army alive.

Comberth Harbor is full of burning ships.

fields.text: The Stonehenge engineers escape
lines: The Stonehenge engineers escape

fields.text:
They came out through the desert at night, families and all.

The official chronology records that the Stonehenge engineers and their families escaped Erusean custody on 14 March 2005. The men and women who built the railguns to save the world from Ulysses are out of Erusean hands. Whatever happens to the battery now, the people who made it are safe.

fields.text: Erusea asks for an armistice
lines: Erusea asks for an armistice

fields.text:
The request came through a neutral embassy, written in the formal language of surrender negotiations without using the word.

Erusea proposes an armistice along the current front lines. Its envoys say that the war has cost both sides more than either can afford, and that the continent needs reconstruction more than it needs a victor. They offer to stop where the armies stand and to talk about everything else afterwards.

Our generals are divided. Some believe Erusea is near breaking and that an armistice now would let it rebuild for another war. Others point to the casualty lists and the empty treasury. Accepting ends the war without a decision. Refusing means fighting on to the end, wherever that is.

fields.text:
ISAF's offer was broadcast openly, so that the Erusean people would hear it at the same time as their government.

The allied command proposes an armistice along the current front lines. The fighting would stop where the armies stand; borders, prisoners and Stonehenge would be settled at a conference afterwards. The offer is generous. It is also a test of whether the government in Farbanti can still afford to say no.

Accepting ends the war without a decision on the battlefield. Refusing commits Erusea to fighting on.

fields.text: Farbanti falls
lines: Farbanti falls

fields.text:
FARBANTI — The Erusean capital has fallen, and the Usean Continental War is over.

Allied columns entered Farbanti's outskirts this week after a final offensive across the continent. The official chronology records that Farbanti fell and Erusea surrendered on 19 September 2005. Reporters describe white sheets hanging from apartment windows, Erusean soldiers stacking their rifles in the squares, and crowds that cannot decide whether to cheer or weep.

Two years after the invasion of San Salvacion, ISAF has done what its critics said it could not. The cost is still being counted: cities damaged in the fighting, a generation of pilots lost, and a continent that came through a falling sky only to tear itself apart.

Allied officers warn that the surrender has not ended every danger. Some Erusean units have not answered the order to lay down arms.

fields.text: Erusea wins the Continental War
lines: Erusea wins the Continental War

fields.text:
The broadcasts from Farbanti have been triumphant for a week.

Central Usea's command has collapsed. Its armies have capitulated or scattered, its allies are seeking terms, and Erusea's forces dominate the continent from San Salvacion to the coast. In the occupied capitals, Erusean administrators are moving into ministries whose previous occupants have fled or been arrested.

In the official chronology, ISAF wins the Continental War. In this campaign Erusea has won it, and the order that follows will be written in Farbanti.

fields.text: An armistice in Usea
lines: An armistice in Usea

fields.text:
The guns along the front have stopped, and nobody has won.

An armistice now holds between Erusea and the allied governments along the front lines as they stood on the day it was signed. Neither side has the strength to break the other, and both have agreed to stop trying, for now. Prisoners will be exchanged and commissions will meet. The maps in every staff headquarters show a line that both sides call temporary.

In the official chronology, ISAF wins the Continental War. In this campaign the war has ended in a stalemate, and the continent will have to live with a border drawn by exhaustion.

fields.text: Megalith
lines: Megalith

fields.text:
The surrender is barely a week old when the reports start coming in.

Young Erusean officers, refusing their government's order to lay down arms, have seized Megalith, a fortress built to bring down orbiting Ulysses fragments. Allied intelligence knows little about it beyond its purpose, and that purpose is enough. A weapon built to bring down fragments of Ulysses is now in the hands of men who refused to surrender.

The official chronology records that young Erusean officers seized Megalith on 26 September 2005. ISAF must take the fortress before it can be used. The pilots chosen for the mission have been told only that it may be the last flight of the war.

fields.text: Megalith is destroyed
lines: Megalith is destroyed

fields.text:
Megalith is silent.

The allied strike group went in under the fortress's defences and came out again with fewer aircraft than it took. The reports from the cockpits are fragmentary and the debriefings run long. Whatever the officers who seized it meant to do, they will not do it now.

The war is over. This time, nobody is broadcasting otherwise.

fields.text: Erusea's provisional government
lines: Erusea's provisional government

fields.text:
Erusea will govern itself again, under oversight.

The official chronology records that after Megalith was destroyed, Erusea formed a provisional autonomous government under ISAF oversight. The new administration has inherited a country with damaged cities, an army in camps and a population that lived through both a falling sky and a lost war in six years.

In this campaign the government in office remains in place. The oversight arrangement is shown as a national spirit, not a change of borders or ideology. What Erusea becomes now is a question for the years after 2005.

fields.text: Usea at the end of the war
lines: Usea at the end of the war

fields.text:
The year closes, and the archivists have started their work.

Refugee pressure stands at [?ac_ucw_pressure|.0]. Fallout recovery stands at [?ac_ucw_recovery|.0]. [GetUcwOutcome]

Six years have passed since Ulysses broke apart over the world. Usea has been shaped by the decisions taken in that time: borders opened or closed, talks accepted or refused, a war fought or averted. Some of the ministries that drafted the first fallout brief no longer exist. Many of the people who walked toward the borders in 2000 have not gone home, and some of them never will.

This is the end of the authored Usean chronology. The campaign continues; what comes next has not yet been written.

fields.text: The Telephone That Everyone Calls
lines: The Telephone That Everyone Calls

fields.text: A district operator has pinned three unofficial numbers beside the official switchboard. They reach the people who can find a water crew, open a shelter or explain why a receiving office is shut. None appears in the national register. Publishing the contact list would make a fragile local arrangement into a public service; keeping it within the rota would leave operators freer to improvise. The choice is who can demand an answer when a familiar voice is no longer there.

fields.text: The Key in the Wrong Office

fields.text: An inspection has found a sound shelter whose key is held by an office that closes before the evening protection rota begins. Everyone involved followed a written instruction. The protection service can fund a joint receiving desk and rebuild institutional capacity, or put dispatchers on an immediate priority footing so the next practical allocation need not wait. Neither course creates more staff; it changes how the existing service uses them.

lines: A Forecast on Every Noticeboard

Dispatch staff ask instead for time to revise the movement chain. The first choice strengthens preparation completed before the crisis boundary; the second improves a military and service capability that remains useful afterward. Neither can promise safety simply by printing a confident sentence.

What cannot be offered is capacity that the country has only counted twice.

The service must choose what it can responsibly promise, rather than declare every missing record found.

lines: The Network's Ordinary Year

fields.text: The national programme now has a record of what survived, what was refused and what had to be done under external conditions. Its conclusion does not decide the war or erase the settlement. The government can renew an ordinary civil service whose future funded completions support recovery, or retain a bounded readiness record at a continuing public cost. Either choice is an ongoing obligation, not a final gift from the calendar.

lines: Two Owners of the Same Timetable

Amber can publish a common record, accepting the public cost of explaining which bargain had to wait, or maintain a restricted operational schedule and concentrate on dispatch capability. The timetable is a development policy before it becomes a relief plan.

lines: A Reserve That Can Say No

fields.text: The reserve authority can now describe its actual limits under the settlement that remains. A useful national programme is one that can refuse a fifth commitment when only four slots exist. The country can renew ordinary service work whose funded completions aid recovery, or retain a readiness record with its continuing public burden. The choice preserves a limited capability rather than an endless emergency.

fields.text: Nation In Pieces
lines: Nation In Pieces

fields.text: Our nation is in pain. The continued overspending on the military has wrecked our economy, which in turn has caused businesses to downsize, laying off workers, making them spend less, further drying up economic growth, causing company after company to close their doors. Without the goods and services offered by many of these companies, it has gotten harder and harder for our citizens to source food, pay bills, or provide for their families. This, in turn, has caused drastically increased radicalization and polarization of our populace, who turn to radical idealisms as their only hope of change. Even worse, due to our nation being in this state for quite some time, even our resources in the government are now beginning to run thin.

fields.text: People On The Streets
lines: People On The Streets

fields.text: The scope of the protests is far greater than we ever imagined. Nearly every day has some kind of major protest happening somewhere in our country, and crimes have also seen exponential growth compared to when this all began. Masses of people are calling for all sorts of demands, from more reform programs all the way to calls for outright revolution. The silver lining in this is that the sheer mass of protesters makes them unable to unite or organize effectively, making them less of a threat than an organized group. Regardless, this will only buy us some time, as if we continue to leave this issue unresolved they will no doubt find a way to organize.

fields.text: Economy Long Gone
lines: Economy Long Gone

fields.text: Our economy has had negative growth for over a year now, and the effects are extremely obvious. The vast majority of our nation lives below the poverty line, as the middle class has been all but obliterated. More than half of the small businesses in the country have closed, and about a third of the large businesses went bankrupt or were bought out. International companies and investors saw the writing on the wall long ago and have left for greener pastures, meaning there's no external group we can use to leverage ourselves back onto our feet. Worst of all, now our own funds in the government have begun to dry up, and we've had to downsize our own government and print larger amounts of currency to offset our expenses. However, even that is wearing thin and the inflation is devaluing our money faster than we can print enough to compensate it.

fields.text: Mass Exodus
lines: Mass Exodus

fields.text: Unemployment is only the tip of the iceberg. Workers, scientists, doctors, lawyers, even our own officials are emigrating to other countries to find work, and at an alarming rate. The lack of job opportunities in Belka is causing workers to look elsewhere, even outside their home country, to provide for their families. Some are even taking their families with them. Houses run empty and border checkpoints are crowded as people scramble to exit the country. Not only have we lost our workforce, but we will be unable to recover them if we cannot stop this outflow of people. If this keeps up, there won't even be a Belka to revive.

fields.text: Complete Collapse
lines: Complete Collapse

fields.text: It appears, ironically, that our last efforts to take inventory on the crisis pushed us over the tipping point. Our budget this month was unable to meet the expenses, and as a result we, as a nation, are in complete bankruptcy. As our officials find out, many are simply getting up and leaving. We are completely powerless and at the whims of whatever the future brings. The only influence we have is off goodwill alone, and that will not get us far. The future is dark.

lines: Government Falls Apart

fields.text: The word is out. The jig is up. Everyone knows about the state of the government, and almost everyone in any position of power has either been forced out or simply walked out. Belka is in a state of anarchy. It is impossible to even tell what is happening in the country because all sources of information we could use is gone or takes orders from someone new now. Dinsmark is empty.

fields.text: New Elections, New Rule
lines: New Elections, New Rule

fields.text: After the collapse of the BCNP's administration, an emergency election was called by the Alternative Wege to regain control of the government. Unsurprisingly, they came out on top, with the BNCP scattered between the DLP, Wege itself, and the rest joining the monarchist movement. With the liberals now in power and promising to fix the mistakes of the past no matter how difficult it may be, a sliver of hope has returned that new leaders may bring about change.

fields.text: Osean Proposition
lines: Osean Proposition

fields.text: Our longtime rival, the Osean Federation, have approached us with an interesting offer. In return for giving several of our eastern territories to the neighboring countries, and selling a portion of the Great Lakes to Osea itself, the Oseans will pay us a rather high sum of money, giving us the ability to start some recovery programs. Osea has even expressed that they would be willing to lease many of the resources in the area to us through a joint resource excavation company. Some in the government are suspicious of this deal, since it's unlikley that Osea would offer us such a deal without a clear benefit to them, but others are hopeful that it could be the beginning of a new era of cooperation between our nations, as well as our lifeline to save our nation. It is a rather humiliating deal to take, but what other choice do we have?

fields.text: Selling Of The Land
lines: Selling Of The Land

fields.text: With all the paperwork in place, we've agreed to the Oseans' proposal and are preparing to remove our forces from the land. The transactions have been made and we now have enough money to get a few programs going. For their cooperation, [BLK.GetLeader] has suggested we take the Oseans up on their joint resource company offer, something that will give us a reliable income from which to rebuild the rest of our country off of.

fields.text: GLRDC Goes Live
lines: GLRDC Goes Live

fields.text: The Great Lakes Resource Development Company opened up today, marking our second cooperation with the Oseans. Early reports have showed us promising amounts of resources in the area, meaning this will likely be a very lucrative deal. Digging has begun and we've invested more of our money into the program to see a profit as quickly as we can. Things are looking up for us, we may just be able to refloat our economy with this.

fields.text: The Results Are In
lines: The Results Are In

fields.text:
They lied to us. 

 The Oseans lied to us about the resources. There weren't even any to begin with in that area. To add insult to injury, we're getting reports in the eastern countries that the territories we sold have plentiful resources in them, that now those countries are exploiting to their full potential. We are now down almost all the money we got from the original deal, and now there does not appear to be any sort of tool or program we can use to save ourselves.

fields.text: Total Anarchy
lines: Total Anarchy

fields.text: After the news of the Osean scam got out, the public has been whirled back into a frenzy, and our attempts at damage control seem to have completely failed. We've run out of money again, and now the [BLK.GetRulingParty] is seeing mass defections to the communists and monarchists. The public is completely uncontrollable and the nation is in complete anarchy.

fields.text: New Power At The Top
lines: New Power At The Top

fields.text: Over the past few days, an intense battle between the DLP and the monarchists ensued across the country, with the DLP now the undisputed dominant power in the country. With the DLP's support in the military assisting them, they have secured control over all apparatuses of state and now are the new leaders of the country, with most of the opposition imprisoned or jailed. With its third government in the last few months, it remains to be seen if the DLP will solve any of the issues plaguing the country.

fields.text: Many People, One Nation, One Goal
lines: Many People, One Nation, One Goal

fields.text: Belka has been wounded, not just by her enemies but also by her own supposed leaders, each of whom pulled her apart seeking their own goals. The failiures of the previous governments showed they were not fit to lead Belka. Now it is our turn. We will unite the people and raise Belka from the ashes, ascendent to the top of the world. With no one left to stand in our way, the DLP will restore Belka to its former glory and beyond. We have much to do, and the people's patience is thin because of the past, so we must waste no time in getting to work. Many of our members have already put forward ideas to start our recovery, which will provide us with a head start on our recovery.

fields.text: The 2 Year Plan
lines: The 2 Year Plan

fields.text: After intense discussion, we have arrived at a conclusion on how to start our reconstruction. While the military is all we have left, and is necessary for our self-preservation, this is exactly what we will use to our advantage. Converting a large amount of our military production into civilan will allow us to start economic growth without many funds to go off of, and our military is powerful enough as it is to ward off any potential invasions from Osea. This will upset the militarist faction in our government, but in all likelyhood they will come around when our economy recovers, which we can use to expand the military from once again.

fields.text: Magic Of Bureaucracy
lines: Magic Of Bureaucracy

fields.text: Through some decisive means, we've found a way to get back at those wretched Oseans. We still technically have a share in the Great Lakes Resource Development Company, but who said we have to use it for that purpose? Using some underhanded methods and pulling strings, we've managed to convert some of the resources used in that project to produce some industry for our own benefit. This will only work for so long before either the Oseans find out and shut down the company, or the company itself dries up, but it's a nice boost, and one that sticks it to the Oseans.

fields.text: Harsh Countermeasures
lines: Harsh Countermeasures

fields.text: Getting jobs for the unemployed is a rather large task, however a mitigation we can use to still get some usable labor is by introducing forced labor and community service for prisoners in our nation. To bolster these numbers, we have criminalized emigration and remaining unemployed, which should hopefully give us an edge against unemployment, at the cost of some public opinion.

fields.text: Regulate Trade Policy
lines: Regulate Trade Policy

fields.text: To recover our economy, we'll need to prompt trade with other nations, but we need to make sure we're gaining a strong profit from it. Rather than allow companies to do free business, we'll make sure that any trade goes through us before it is approved, allowing us to take a cut of the sale, letting us improve the economy itself. With any luck, this process will repeat exponentially, encouraging investors despite the tax of our government on their transactions.

fields.text: Clashes Within The Party
lines: Clashes Within The Party

fields.text: We always expected opposition, at least from the public, and from within our own party to an extent, but we didn't expect it to be around this long. We've begun a number of recovery programs and are already seeing the first fruits of recovery, and yet the militarist faction of our government led by Waldemarr Rald has only dissented louder and louder with each reform that we make, cutting into the military's budget. Unfortunately for us, many of the close-minded officers and generals in the Belkan Armed Forces are seeing these budget cuts as attacks on their livelihood and siding with Rald. It's begun to affect our ability in decision-making, meaning we'll likely need to find a way to please Rald and his militarists.

fields.text: Support In The Military
lines: Support In The Military

fields.text: Almost as soon as we began discussing possible resolutions with Rald, he seems to have disappeared, as well as most of his supporters. We're unsure if they're plotting something, are attempting to force our cabinet into stasis by not meeting the seat count, or if they simply gave up, but in any case it seems the issue resolved itself. Worryingly, many of the heads of the Armed Forces have come forward announcing support for Rald, but despite this outflow of support he has yet to make any appearances.

fields.text: The Coup
lines: The Coup

fields.text: Ein Volk, Ein Nation, Ein Ziel!
lines: Ein Volk, Ein Nation, Ein Ziel!

fields.text: President Rald held a public speech today, calling for the Belkan people to put aside their differences and remember that they are, above all else, Belkans, and that is what matters. Nationalism has always been high after the Osean scam in the Great Lakes, and it seems Rald is capitalizing on this, uniting the people under their nationality. This has alarmed several nations around us, mostly Osea and our former member nations, but domestically this speech has seen Rald's approval ratings increase greatly.

fields.text: Total War
lines: Total War

fields.text: The humliation and shame inflicted on us not just by Osea, but also the foolish conservatives who allowed Belkan territory to secede in the 1987 Federal Law Review, cannot be allowed to stand. Waldemarr Rald held a meeting with his cabinet today promising an immenent revenge war against Osea and the former states, reclaiming lost Belkan territory, as soon as the military is restored back to its former level. While he has not gone public with this information, he has constantly blamed Osea and the other nations for poisoning Belka, and promises citizens that things will be made right. Rald promises to his cabinet a state of 'total war,' as he describes it- 'To wage war with all tools, methods, resources, and weapons that you have at your disposal, to fight tooth and nail with everything you have until victory or annhilation.'

fields.text: Excalibur Online
lines: Excalibur Online

fields.text: Excalibur, the chemical laser anti-ICBM system devised as a part of the large military build-up of the past couple decades, has finally been finished with our efforts. The designs have changed slightly since the original proposed design from 1981, however the core design has remained mostly unchanged. These designs have allowed us to make the design more modular, including swappable lenses for different ranges and targets, as well as heat transferring pipes to allow the main structure to assist in cooling as well as the six primary cooling towers. This also has allowed for possible future improvements on the design, but for now we have a simple choice to make on where to invest the last of the project's leftover budget. We could develop an electronic targeting system that syncs up with radar data, allowing Excalibur to easily target agile objects like aircraft, boosting our air superiority capabilities. We could even invest in a denser power system, allowing the laser to reach higher temperatures and give it the ability to assist in ground attacks. Or we could simply keep it to its original purpose and improve its ICBM destruction capabilities.

fields.text: Got Mitt Uns
lines: Got Mitt Uns

fields.text: Religion is a large part of people's lives in Belka, and for the church to disagree with the state would cause dissent within the nation. To combat this, Waldemarr Rald has decided to declare the United Church of Belka, to ensure that the church does not teach dissenting thoughts against the state. This new organization will need a leader from the religious sector that will not be seen as a mere puppet. The three best possible candidates have been presented to Rald, and we now await his answer. Father Hannes Kellermann, head of the Church of Dinsmark, has been an outspoken loyalist of the DLP and while he was originally supportive of the pacifist wing of the party, has since come around and speaks extremely positively of Rald. He may not be very useful aside from his high charisma and undying loyalty, but the church will never be an issue as long as he is around. Opposite of him is Father Arnold Weinmann, a leading figure in the Lumen Cathedral, originally a member of the Alternative Wege, but reluctantly changed to the DLP after accusations of Osean sympathies. He is not an Osean sympathizer, however he greatly prefers the pacifist wing of the DLP, and has yet to endorse Rald publicly, making his loyalty questionable. Despite that, he used to work as an economist during the military build-up several years ago, and likely could be of use in that area, assisting with our own build-up. Finally, we have Father Wilfried Jan Riese von Sergio Luoni, a former bishop from Hoffnung, who was removed from position after declaring many sects as heretical and claiming only he had the true interpretation of the Scriptures. He has since been excommunicated, but leads a small cult-like following in Sudentor, mostly popular with lower-class people and occultists. He is a wild card, loyalty unknown and likely would not serve any extra benefits, however his leadership would keep the Church far from government affairs, as it would be too busy fighting itself to make any targeted effort agains the government.

fields.text: New Generals
lines: New Generals

fields.text: Expanding our military will require expanding command just as much as recruiting more soldiers, and for that we must make a choice of where our new leaders will come from. Some younger members of the DLP are involved with the Belkan Army, and while they may not be the cream of the crop, their ideological loyalty may be worth it if a campaign does not go well, where a lesser general may retreat or surrender. Alternatively, the Belkan Officer Academy always allows the best to rise to the top, however the students there belong to a wide variety of ideologies, and as such their quality might be offset by their loyalty to our cause.

lines: Belka Uber Alles

fields.text: The idea of Belka must be firmly rooted in the mind of each soldier, worker, and citizen of Belka. Not the Belka of today, not the government of Belka nor its people or its land. Belkans must be obsessed with the idea of a Belka that is greater than anything we could imagine now. Closer than family, than work, than religion, than life itself. So close that they are willing to fight, work and die to achieve it. Raising Belka to the status of a deity that we owe our lives, that we must serve with all we have. A Belka that is timeless and infinite, a Belka that is strong to its core. A Belka over all.

lines: Martial Law

fields.text: Martial law is rolling out all over Belkan cities, tightening our grip on the state of affairs in our country. With expanded police forces, curfews, and routine patrols, we can monitor any potential threats to our future decisions very easily. A complete survelliance and police state can be easily controlled and run like a well-oiled machine, and any issues can be brought directly to us within hours.

fields.text: Formation of The BSF
lines: Formation of The BSF

fields.text: The Belkan Special Forces, taking spirit from the ancient Belkan Royal Guard, has been fully formed and now the best soldiers and officers from across the nation are being handpicked to stock its ranks. Highly disciplined and routinely tested to stay in top shape, the BSF will be both the spearhead in any attack in war, and the centerpoint in any critical defense. No doubt will the BSF set a precedent for elite divisions around the world, and we hope to expand its size and capabilities in the coming times.

fields.text: Resources in Ustio
lines: Resources in Ustio

fields.text: Yesterday, a news report was published in Ustio detailing mass deposits of precious metals beneath the surface of its mountains, extremely close to the surface, with the land market exploding overnight. Rald is beside himself with fury at the news, claiming that Ustio should cede all resource rights to Belka, as the resources had not been discovered when the conservatives foolishly allowed the Ustians to secede. With the new money, Ustio has already announced several new programs to stabilize themselves, much to our dismay. A small paper trail suggests that Osea might also have been intentionally hiding these resources until Ustio declared its independence, also lending credibility to the theory that Osea funded Ustian independence movements as well. Rald has declared to his cabinet that this has been the last straw, and is preparing the military for imminent war within the next six months.

fields.text: Attack on Excalibur
lines: Attack on Excalibur

fields.text: Excalibur, our chemical laser anti-ICBM weapon, has been destroyed in a massive raid by the Osean Air Defense Force and Ustian Air Force, completely eliminating its viability. Despite massive losses and fierce resistance from our forces, the four RTLS systems and the surrounding support weapons were slowly picked off by the aircraft, before destroying the lens itself, then finally targeting the central structure until it collapsed, rendering it completely unsalvageable. While we still own the territory underneath Excalibur, the weapon is completely unusable and would not be repairable without a complete rebuilding of the structure. While this does not mean a complete loss, this will greatly set back our ability to project power around our nation, and we will need to be much more careful about which battles we have the capacity to fight in the future.

fields.text: The Belkan War
lines: The Belkan War

fields.text:
The Belkan War was a large scale conflict that took part between the 25th of March, 1995 and June 20th of the same year. It involved two of the largest superpowers of the world, being the bellicose nation of Belka and the Osean Federation with addition of all other Belkan neighbors. It all started after an unprecedented economic crisis hit Belka a decade earlier, leading to territorial concessions and a desperate population to seek hope and revenge in a far-right, militarist party, who used all Belka's remaining economic might to wage war against Ustio, a country that recently seceded and found enormous amounts of resources.

Thus, Belka declared war on all surrounding countries in a last-ditch attempt to gain supremacy in the Osean continent and regain all lost territories. After an initial setback, the attacked countries formed an alliance that counterattacked and pushed back Belkan forces, expoliting the inability of Belkan state to sustain equipment losses. With rumors, later confirmed, of Belka developing weapons of mass destruction, Allied forces continued to penetrate Belkan lands leading to the secession of the southern part of the nation, until the Belkan government, in a desperate attempt to save the northern part of the country, launched a nuclear attack along the Waldreich Mountains on June 6th, 1995.

Seeing the insanity unfold, the Allies accepted Belka's sue for peace resulting in the peace conference of Lumen of June 20th.

fields.text: Drums of War
lines: Drums of War

fields.text: Desperation
lines: Desperation

fields.text: As much as it burns to admit, the outcome of this war is not looking in our favor. Our casualties have grown dangerously high both from a tactical and civilian perspective, and we are losing ground and resources rapidly, made even worse by the sudden defection of South Belka. To say the situation is dire is an understatement. If nothing is done, we must end the war, else we are ousted from power. However, we may have one final option to still prevent complete surrender. We still possess the two V2 MIRV nuclear missile systems we developed as the result of Project Pendragon, as well as many V1 nuclear warheads that can still be utilized. To use these weapons against Osea or their allies would be to spell death for ourselves, as nuclear retaliation would be inevitable. However, a desperate, but possible plan has been proposed: Detonating seven nuclear warheads at key pass points in the Waldreich mountain range would either force the Allied Forces to either move through the mountain range itself, or through an irradiated wasteland. It is a costly move, one that will hurt our image greatly, and shock and horrify both our citizens and people worldwide, but this shock will grant us our survival. None will wish to continue fighting us if they see how dedicated we are to our survival. We will not win this war, but we will not let Osea win either.

fields.text: Ground Zero
lines: Ground Zero

fields.text: All preparations for the operation are set. All seven nuclear warheads have been primed and are in their proper locations. All that awaits now is to make the final order, and Belka shall be bathed in the light of eight suns. This action will put fear into the hearts of our people and the people of other nations alike, as nothing like this has ever been done in the history of the world. They will be shocked and horrified, and that will be our only chance. After the nuclear detonations, we must end the war immediately before their fear turns to fury. It is our last chance at the survival of Belkan honor. The only struggle after that will be keeping our nation afloat after this is done, as while we can drive off the invaders, we must regain the trust of the people for what we have done. It will be a long and bloody road, but we will finish what we started.

fields.text: Peace with Shame
lines: Peace with Shame

fields.text: A humiliating peace deal, but it allows our survival. The negotiations, signed in Lumen yesterday, cede the entirety of the demilitarized South Belka to Osea, finally completing their century-long conquest of the Great Lakes. While we are forced to return the territory we sold to the eastern nations, they do not gain any new territory, and South Belka is our only territorial loss. However, this is more than made up in the enormous quantity of reparations owed to all nations involved, despite our already pitiful economic state. To add insult to injury, massive limitations have been placed on our pride, the Belkan Armed Forces, limiting our soldiers, equipment, and research capabilities. If that wasn't enough, Osea will not return any companies, factories, or any kind of value in South Belka to us, leaving us even less tools to rebuild. Despite this extreme humiliation and defeat, we have managed to conceal the existence of the Avalon Dam facility as well as our remaining nuclear stockpile. Debate now remains on if we should use these weapons to enact a final revenge on Osea, even if it causes our demise, or using these tools to maintain our independence as we enter the next era. With the debates still ongoing, the future is unsure, but at last, war is over for now.

fields.text: Oseans Sue For Peace
lines: Oseans Sue For Peace

fields.text: President Rald and several high-ranking members of our cabinet were formally invited to Carbonero today to write a peace treaty, ending the state of war between Belka and Osea. Due to mounting casualties and increasing pressure from their public, Osea has had no choice but to cave into the public's demands, and is now seeking an exit from the war. Once again proving liberalism's failure, Osea's hand has been twisted by their own people, just as it was in 1910. The conditions on Osea were harsh but not crushing, as while we are winning, we too need to end the war quickly before our own supplies run out, as well as Rald is being cautious to not bite off more than we can chew. The main terms of surrender are Osea surrendering all of their recently stolen territories to us, fully revoking their claims on the Great Lake territory, and signing a pact of non-intervention over all Eastern Osean nations except Sapin, in addition to an extremely large sum of war reparations. Osea has begrudgingly agreed to these terms, rendering us free from their meddling for the time being. All that remains now is to clean up the eastern front, and we will have near-free reign over Eastern Osea.

fields.text: Peace with Triumph
lines: Peace with Triumph

fields.text: Though the battle was long and filled with strife, we have righted the wrongs of the past and Belka stands atop her place with the rest of the world powers. Lost territory has been reclaimed, with new puppet regimes in FATO, Gebet, and Recta to serve us, as well as new plunder from Osea giving us control over the Great Lakes and Futuro Canal. Osea has been beaten back to lick their wounds, and will have a much harder time challenging us in the future. With nothing left that can easily topple us, we are now free to pursue any claims or injustices we wish to rectify. Despite our victory, much of our nation has suffered, as well as our new conquests need much repair. But now, with new influence and resources at our fingertips, strengthening our armed forces as well as rebuilding our economy will be easier than ever before. Victory parades are rampant across Belka, and we look boldly to the future as we sign the next chapter in the history of the world, this one penned by the great nation of Belka.

wish to rectify. Despite our victory, much of our nation has suffered, as well as
our new conquests need much repair. But now, with new influence and
resources at our fingertips, strengthening our armed forces as well as
rebuilding our economy will be easier than ever before. Victory parades are
rampant across Belka, and we look boldly to the future as we sign the next
chapter in the history of the world, this one penned by the great nation of Belka.

Military and economic departments must work under the revised emergency measures, while our neighbours receive their own assessments of the situation. Mobilisation cannot make those pressures disappear.

fields.text: Economic Troubles
lines: Economic Troubles

fields.text: The economic reforms made by the pacifists hurt our armed forces, however it did contribute to our economic growth. After Rald began to rebuild the military, the economy did not pitfall, however it has been stagnating for a while, and we are starting to dip back downward. While we are able to control this directly using our authority, nullifying the effects, we must immediately gain resources to our economy upon invading our foes, as we won't be able to hold the floodgates forever. We will start strong, but if we cannot secure loot to continue our war efforts, our civilian infrastructure will collapse in on itself, giving way to our military collapsing as well. Until then, we will fight with what we have been able to amass thus far.

fields.text: While we have been able to keep economic troubles down from our manual control over several aspects of life, the cracks are beginning to show, and our ability to manage industry and civilian infrastructure is beginning to slip. It is still currently manageable, but we must find a new source of income else we lose control of the situation.

fields.text: Collapse of Order
lines: Collapse of Order

fields.text: The economic situation has fallen out of our grasp and now we are paying the consequences in full. The state of civilian life has returned to depression status, and we are losing contact with several locations around our nation. While the instability has not yet reached our military, desertions by public servants, protests, and layoffs is severely limiting our ability to supply them properly, and if we do not get some sort of damage control immediately, it is unlikely we will be able to control our military.

Civilian works, military production and naval construction all face cuts, while the army is to be reduced under the existing programme. Carrying out those orders will reshape the capacity available to the government.

fields.text: Intervention
lines: Intervention

fields.text:
We knew about huge opposition to war in some parts of the military, especially in South Belkan and forces connected to Liberal politicians. We knew that at some point they would betray our Fatherland and run away like cowards - exactly what they did not long ago.

But we were blind to another group of military officials hiding and planning under the noses of everyone else. We were thinking that we - true sons of North Belka - are real patriots without equal. Only we knew how to protect Belka or whatever will remain from it.

But today we were proven wrong.

In a span of mere minutes after the military high command meeting and authorizing the nuclear detonations, we were all in handcuffs. We thought it was part of the plan of traitors from the South but we could not be more far from the truth. For them abandoning half of the country, abandoning the glory of Belka in shameful defeat, abandoning our pride - was ultimate treason to the state. For to be Belkan is to march forward with head high into even darkest of the nights on stormy seas. It was us who were blind, wanting to preserve what would become a dead corpse without its spirit.

To them, if Belka is to die it should do it with a sword in hand, fighting like it always did, refusing to go quietly into that good night.

fields.text: Sunset of Belka
lines: Sunset of Belka

fields.text:
Our soldiers have been briefed. The defense lines have been set. The conscripts have been raised. The guns are aimed southward. Those cowards though tarnishing our beautiful land with nuclear fire would be the answer. No. We are better than that. They want to control Belka's people, manipulate them. They cannot do that if there are no people to control. We will show them, and the world, what sets Belkans apart from the rest of the world. We will never stop fighting, until the last man dies, until the last bullet is fired, until the last shell is spent. If they so badly want our home, they will need to pry it from our grip. There is only one objective.

Hold the line at all costs.

fields.text: Our tardiness in preparing for the Osean onslaught has doomed us. The Oseans have already arrived, and our defenses have not been fully prepared, and as a result we cannot fully defend our positions. No matter what benefit we may have from our current progress, it will not be enough. All that remains now is to watch what remains of our forces be swept away by the Allied Forces. Many of the officers in charge of the operation have comitted suicide before they can be arrested by the Allied Forces.

fields.text: Osea Backs Down
lines: Osea Backs Down

fields.text: After a extended absence of attacks on our defensive line, we recieved news from Osea that they wish to sign a peace treaty with us. This has come as a bit of a surprise, as the dire state of our nation was rather obvious to the Oseans, and our goal was to merely take as many of them with us as possible. However, this offer has presented us with an interesting opportunity. We had thought that there was no way out, and that Belka was lost no matter what, but we may still come out on top with a peace treaty at a time like this. Some still want to fight to the last breath, and consider peace with Osea treason, however living to fight another day may give us another chance to defeat Osea, whereas continuing to fight would no doubt end in our complete destruction. Regardless, the peace offer is a clear sign that our goal of causing as much damage to the Oseans as possible has largely succeeded.

fields.text: The Fire Fades
lines: The Fire Fades

fields.text: Despite our best efforts, the Allied Forces have punctured our defensive line. From here they can push into North Belka proper, as well as flank our troops from the side, circumventing our defensive preparations. Putting all our resources into this last defensive line, we have nothing left to defend the cities and towns besides small garrisons and civil units. Now we can do nothing but resign ourselves to fate as every last defender of Belka is slaughtered at the hands of the Oseans. Belka is lost.

fields.text: Peace with Survival
lines: Peace with Survival

fields.text: We expected annhilation. We expected destruction and torture on earth, and to be casted into the deepest pits of hell following our death. However, unknowingly, we have saved Belka. Following multiple failed attempts at breaching our line, Osea's casualties appear to have reached so high that they could no longer afford to keep fighting, and have requested to sue for peace with us. While we did force their hand into peace, this is not exactly a victory, as we had to accept Osean ownership of the stolen lands, as well as take responsibility for the war through reparations. Still, this is a better outcome than hoped, and Belka as a nation remains. Not only that, but we have proven to the world how hard we will fight to defend our land. The officers that defied orders to perform the operation have been pardoned for their actions, although many are critical of how many lives were spent in the process.

fields.text: Belkan Victory
lines: Belkan Victory

fields.text: Despite being in the deepest depression the nation had ever seen. Despite suffering 4 goverment changes in the span of a few years. Despite being backstabbed, surrounded, and it's military neutered, Belka has won. Osea has sued for peace after facing mounting backlash at home about the war being pointless now that the Eastern Osean nations have been occupied, and blaming their government for failing to protect them. Sapin has pulled back with them, the casualties on it's military leaving it compromised and even more reliant on the Oseans than before. The East lies under our control, at least formally, and as it stands today, Belka is the mightiest nation on the continent.

fields.text: Belka Day
lines: Belka Day

fields.text: Morale and patriotism are reaching all time peaks as the people come out in droves, not to protest, but this time to celebrate the great victory over those who would see us undone. Our people, military, and government are elated and optimistic for the future, and Waldemarr Rald has called both for a official holiday every year on the day of the treaty, and a nearly month-long celebration right now to commemorate our great victory. Additionally, Rald is preparing both the largest military parade in the world to date, as well as a fiery speech to the people of the nation.

fields.text: Formal resistance and all semblence of independence in our regained core territories have all but been dismantled, however many infuriated partisans, many of whom were made of the former independence force, have moved underground and have started to fight more covertly against our rule. Much of the industry and infrastructure has been utterly decimated, as it was already rundown as a result of the depression, making it very weak to the fighting during the war, in addition to intentional destructions by the resistance as they retreated. Most of the non-Belkans in the area do not share in the sense of celebration the rest of our nation is enjoying, and as a result are not eager to begin rebuilding. It will be a long time before these former lands will be a core part of Belka again.

fields.text: Ustian Occupation
lines: Ustian Occupation

fields.text: The knife that the Oseans used to backstab us, Ustio, has come under our control once again. Rather than being granted regional independence like the Gebetians and Rectans, a combination of their betrayal and the newly discovered resource deposits have led us to fully annex their lands instead. The steel deposits will be used to bolster our own mining operations, and the precious uranium caches will allow us to continue nuclear research, become a profitable export, and possibly develop more powerful superweapons. The downside to this is that the Ustians, whom have always been highly resistant to our rule, only become more radicalized by our annexation, and even though their army was defeated news is coming in of terror attacks and partisan strikes up and down the territory. It will likely be a long time before we can fully pacify and integrate these lands once again.

fields.text: Rebuilding Excalibur?
lines: Rebuilding Excalibur?

fields.text: Because of our proficiency in the war, Excalibur never had to be used to assist us, continuing to keep it's existence a secret. It remains as an anti-ICBM facility in the event of a suprise attack against us, however now with our additional resources and time, we will likely be able to upgrade Excalibur beyond it's original purpose, also extending it's operational range, potentially even using it as a offensive weapon. The lack of use has allowed the facility to stay in tip-top shape without major efforts being put forward to maintain it.

fields.text: The use of Excalibur against our enemies, while revealing it's existence and purpose, was critical in the war effort and it is very clear that it was well worth the effort. With the war now over, and new resources and time on our hands, the potential to upgrade the weapon far past it's initial expectations is beginning to come within our reach. Using the operational data from the war, we know exactly where it's strengths and weaknesses lie, and will be able to work around this information to our advantage.

fields.text: While the destruction of Excalibur was unfortunate, its limited time in operation combined with the effort expended by the Oseans to destroy it has given us a sizable base of knowledge on how to improve on the first design. While the first tower is completely unsalvageable aside from the cooling towers and some of the base components, the site itself is still very usable and while it still will take a large effort to rebuild it, it will still go faster than a complete rebuild in a new location. That, combined with what we learned, will ensure the second Exalibur does not end the same way as the first.

fields.text: Berthold Lehmann Pardoned
lines: Berthold Lehmann Pardoned

fields.text: Berthold Lehmann, the founder of the DLP and the man whom we deposed a few years prior, has been in prison for the duration of the war, to prevent possible meddling in internal affairs during our time of crisis. As the founder of the DLP, he holds enormous sway over the party and it's policies, and was such killing him could destroy our support base. Without a cause to unite us however, holding Lehmann in prison for longer will only serve as more fuel for disunity, and so President Rald has seen it fit to pardon and release him. It is likely he will immediately oppose us for our actions and policies, however our salvation of Belka and triumph over Osea has demanded his respect, and as a result he has agreed to respect Rald as the current term's President, as well as keep the DLP as one party. Now released, Lehmann has once again entered politics, with the hope of winning the next election. In addition to Lehmann, many other members of the DLP have been released as well.

fields.text: Martial Law Revoked

fields.text: Martial law is excellent for maintaining control, but is unsustainable in the long run. Seeing as we have cleared all threats, we have reversed our decision of martial law and are resuming civilian rule over many parts of our nation. As the people return to form however, the critics of our rule have come out of the woodworks, siding with Lehmann and bringing to light many injustices and corrupt actions that occured as a result of our martial law and assertive rule over the nation. As unfortunate as this is, it is preferable to holding martial law indefinitely and having discontent sown silently among the people.

fields.text: Due to efforts by the Gebetian government to tax the Gebetian aristocracy in order to fund social programs designed to uplift Gebet's lower classes, many frustrated Gebetian aristocrats have decided to pack up their bags, liquidate their assets, and leave for Belka. Though this will, in the long-term, result in an overall lower stranglehold by the aristocracy over Gebet's government, many of these aristocrats ran major businesses that employed hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of Gebetians who are now out of a job since their companies have just been liquidated.

While this has led to explosive GDP growth, it's also led to rampant wealth inequality in Gebet.

fields.text: A Taste of Their Own Medicine
lines: A Taste of Their Own Medicine

fields.text:
Flying high above [faulmann_raid_victim.GetName], Faulmann analyzed his on-board optics, scanning for and mentally marking targets for his raid. He'd been able to avoid detection by the Belkans by using the IFF frequency in his plane from back in his days in the Belkan Air Force.

He made sure to make a point with his attack. He'd defected from the Belkan Air Force after a brutal Belkan bomber raid on a Rectan civilian center during the Rectan War. He'd watched the bombers carpet the city in napalm bombs to root out what they believed were rebel forces.

This time, things would be different. He wouldn't stoop to their level. He'd do what he'd gotten his callsign for doing, hitting them with precision strikes on strictly military targets.

After his run was successful, he started flying away from the burning wrecks of military equipment, logistics hubs, and railroads and began heading home. It was then he saw some planes fly behind him on his radar. Turning to see who the Belkans had sent to pursue him, he saw the liveries of his old Belkan squadron. The planes also seemed to recognize him as they kept a lock on him and held it there without firing.

This continued until he went outside of Belkan radar range, at which point each of the planes pursuing him launched a single missile harmlessly into the distance and turned back towards Belka, allowing Faulmann to land safely.

fields.text: 1991 Defense White Paper
lines: 1991 Defense White Paper

fields.text:
The National Security Council has released the 1991 Defense White Paper outlining what Osea's defense strategy will be for the upcoming decade.

The paper focuses on the Yuktobanian threat across the Ceres Ocean and the need for the Osean Defense Forces to focus on developing its aerial and naval forces to control the Ceres Ocean and soften up the Yuktobanian coastline for a potential amphibious invasion.

fields.text: Campaign Season
lines: Campaign Season

fields.text:
As 1991 draws to a close, the people's minds begin to turn to the election due in July of next year. Incumbent President Daniel Andrews of the Unity Party has seen good success throughout his presidency, and seeing as this is merely his first term, the Unity Party is riding on his re-election with a high probability of success. Andrews' Rearmament Declaration at the start of his presidency followed by his comittment to safeguard Osean interests around the globe kicked off his reputation well, and the recent political defeat of Belka, removing a longtime rival of Osea and fulfilling a century-old promise to the Great Lakers simutaneously has greatly increased his popularity with the more hawkish and hardline conservatives, giving him a sizable lead off the Liberty Party. For his second term, Andrews has promised full integration of the Great Lake territories, as well as using their newfound breathing room from Belka to redirect pressure to the Union of Yuktobanian Republics, giving Osea a significant lead in the Cold War.

Opposing Andrews is the Liberty Party's new candidate, Tyler Mackenzie. One of the youngest candidates to ever be chosen, Mackenzie strongly believes that Belka's large military, nationalistic tendencies, and close proximity to Osea makes them a much greater threat than Yuktobania, who he argues Osea should be seeking detente with, instead of carrying the Cold War on into the 21st century. As it stands now, Mackenzie does not have a strong platform to go off of, and the standings are weighted heavily in Andrews' favor currently.

fields.text: The Perblan Menace
lines: The Perblan Menace

fields.text: Our southern neighbor, the Kingdom of Perbla, has never been on good terms with us. With wars commonplace between them and a predecessor nation of ours, the National Republic of Shannon, it's understandable that they would not be amicable to us. Worse still, this has led them to pursue friendly relations with our rival Belka, forming a deadly alliance that skewers us from two angles. The narrowness of the border and the relative state of peace that has existed for some time now has led many to forget the potential threat a Perblan attack has on the heartland of our nation. President Andrews has started a media campaign reminding Oseans of the threat to our south, putting our citizens into a far more hawkish mood, especially those living in our southern regions, as well as swaying them in our favor, showing that we care about their safety and wellbeing from foreign threats.

fields.text: A New Platform

fields.text: Over the past few weeks, Mackenzie's popularity in the polls has been slowly creeping upwards. What seemed like a landslide seems to have slid back into a toss-up, as Mackenzie's predictions about Belka seem to become truer by the day, President Andrews can no longer be sure of his re-election. The Unity Party has been performing massive stunts to swing the public's attention away from Belka and onto Yuktobania, but as the Liberty Party throws everything behind Mackenzie and the truth of Belka's situation seems to become more obvious, it's unlikely they'll be able to pretend nothing is happening for long. Admitting to the truth however, would prove Mackenzie's accusations right, and would be a possibly unrecoverable blow to President Andrews' popularity.

fields.text: The 1992 Osean Federal Elections
lines: The 1992 Osean Federal Elections

fields.text: Today is the day. Ballot boxes all over Osea are stuffed to the brim by eager voters wishing to make their voice heard in the upper halls of Bright Hill. A tight toss-up between Andrews and Mackenzie, with no clear winner discernable from polls, citizens have no choice but to sit in anticipation for the final results to be announced. The media has been greatly enjoying the tension of this election, with exclusive interviews, polls, and event coverage raking in millions of viewers. Voting went mostly smoothly throughout the nation, aside from local incidents and a noteworthy disturbance at an rural Oured ballot box caused by OPP troublemakers. However, as the day draws to a close, and the votes are all tallied, the people of Osea finally hear, as the last ballot is counted, that the winner of the election is...

fields.text: President Mackenzie Elected
lines: President Mackenzie Elected

fields.text: As the results were tallied, the numbers were extremely close but it appears that Tyler Mackenzie has edged out the incumbent Daniel Andrews just barely, securing the presidency for the Liberty Party for the next term. Initial reports were contested and several recounts were performed at the demand of the President, however the results were clear. While not initially having a sizable platform against Andrews, his blunder against Belka last year opened an opportunity for Mackenize to make several predictions about Belka, which quickly began to take shape, making the former President look rather foolish. This upset has gotten extensive media attention, and many are praising Mackenzie as the hero of an underdog story. As the preparations for transfer of power are made, Mackenzie is expected to be inagurated within the next month.

fields.text: The Inaguration of President Mackenzie
lines: The Inaguration of President Mackenzie

fields.text: Tyler Mackenzie was inagurated today as the new President of the Osean Federation. As a member of the Liberty Party, Mackenzie has a large focus on maintaining and expanding individual rights and the rights of the Commonwealths. Most notably, he has a large focus on urban welfare programs, hoping to reduce crime, homelessness, and other issues within large urban centers. While this does leave rural areas somewhat by the wayside, Mackenzie also has plans for large transportations reforms, making it easier to travel throughout the country. In terms of foreign police, Mackenzie is much the opposite of his predecessor, seeking detente with the Union of Yuktobanian Republics, and while originally encouraging cooperation with Belka, after the rise of the DLP he has switched to a hostile stance on them, declaring the DLP to be imprisoning and poisoning the Belkan people. Reactions to this result have been mixed, with the main backlash coming from the Unity Party and our allies, who believe Mackenzie to be an inexperienced, weak-kneed pacifist and communist sympathizer, while many liberal citizens and other nations breathe a sigh of relief from Andrews' hawkishness.

fields.text: The Perblan Problem
lines: The Perblan Problem

fields.text: The Perblan threat to the south is a peculiar one. The Perblans, though nominally neutral, are openly friendly to governments that are actively hostile towards us. That combined with their rapid military buildup has concerned many members of the Osean intelligence community. In the event of a Belkan attack, it's possible that Perbla will support them indirectly, or even directly if they so choose. It would be wise to keep an eye on them during the coming times, and be ready for any possible escalation they may cause.

fields.text: The Yuktobanian Problem
lines: The Yuktobanian Problem

fields.text: Despite our relaxation of tensions from Mackenzie's election, this does not mean we are allies. For years now, the Yuktobanians and Oseans have been in a cold war with each other, vying for influence across the planet to spread their ideologies, propped up by massive technological and armament drives to outpace the other. Should a hot war break out between us and Yuktobania, the primary battlefield will be the Ceres Ocean and many national security advisors are concerned that the Maritime Defense Forces might not be able to achieve a decisive victory over the Yuktobanian Navy, whom we have not been able to get an accurate force reading on.

fields.text: The Mackenzie Doctrine
lines: The Mackenzie Doctrine

fields.text: Osea's foreign policy doctrine has been hyper-focused on containing and combatting Yuktobania, even to the point of having the OIA meddle in Yuktobania itself. However, this tunnel-visioned policy has left Osea blind to other threats that have risen up across the globe. We need to engage in a new policy that decisively reacts to any threat that rises against Osean interests across the globe.

fields.text: Belkan Troubles
lines: Belkan Troubles

fields.text: A couple days ago, the government of the Belkan Federation, our neighbor and rival, became bankrupt and the the residing conservative BNCP was ousted, allowing the more liberal Alternative Wege to seize power. If it was not clear enough, Belka is in an extremely unstable state right now, and it's nearly impossible to predict where the country could be heading next. Given both their desperate situation, and the friendliness towards our country expressed by the new President, Niklaus Weber, some advisors have presented a plan for an opportunity to spin the situation to our advantage to President Andrews.

fields.text: A Pivotal Choice
lines: A Pivotal Choice

fields.text:
The first stage of our plan has gone excellently, and the Belkans are none the wiser. Niklaus Weber is under our thumb. However, this itself has presented a new opportunity, and there is much division in our inner circles on which option is more beneficial. The original plan involves setting up a joint resource company in our recently purchased territories, which, as we know, posess little to no natural resources. This would dry up all of Belka's money from our trade deal, throwing them back into poverty once again. After this, it would only be a matter of time before Belka either loses control of its military or liquidates it, leaving them as a destabilized minor power of little significance to us, allowing us to fully focus on curbing Yuktobania.

The other plan, proposed by some of the more liberal members, would be to instead base the company in Ustio, where we have gotten reports of vast underground resources. Doing this would prove our honesty to the Belkans, allowing us to gain favor with them, and as some have suggested, even a possible alliance. This would also most likely put the Belkans back on their feet, restabilizing them under the Alternative Wege, the government most friendly to us.

Debate is rampant in Bright Hill on which plan to choose, with tensions reaching paramount heights. The former option is more reliable in the initial stages, and would gurantee the largest gain from us, as well as allow us to take the real resources in Ustio for ourselves, and prevent Belka from potentially backstabbing us when recovered. However, plunging Belka back into chaos will cause a great amount of unpredictability, and the situation could develop extremely poorly if not managed well. On the other hand, the latter option is highly variable and could result in either a signifcantly worse or a significantly better outcome than the first plan. It has the potential to portray us globally as a peacemaker and forgiver, increasing our support abroad compared to the Yuktobanians. In addition, the possibility of a stable Belka as our ally would be a large blow to Yuktobanian influence, as we would be completely uncontested in the entire Osean continent. Not to mention how big of an asset Belkan scientists and commanders would be to our nation. However, none of this is guranteed, and the possibility always exists that the Belkans will backstab us or demand the return of their territory once they are stabilized. It's unlikely for them to forget our near century of rivalry, after all. This would also mean we would get a smaller cut of the Ustian resources as well. Lastly, many Oseans do not like the prospect of cooperation with Belka. Our land purchase, while praised for it's benefits, was criticized by more nationalistic groups of our nation, proclaiming we owe Belka nothing and should have simply invaded the territories. These people would likely be in high opposition if we were to continue dealings with Belka, a sentiment reinforced by the Nationalist Union members in our own government. As a result, there is likely to be sizable backlash for our actions if we take this route. Unable to reach a consensus, the final decision rests with the President.

fields.text: Belkan Resistance in the Great Lakes
lines: Belkan Resistance in the Great Lakes

fields.text: While we may have promised liberation to the old owners of this land, that was a rather long time ago and the truth is that the majority of people who live there now mostly consider themselves Belkans through and through. Because of this, only days after moving in we are already recieving reports of protests and discontent with our regime. This was expected, of course, but will take some time to deal with. Eventually we will formally integrate these annexed territories into our federal system, however the region will need to cool off before that can be done. The locals have been living in near poverty from the Belkan Economic Crisis, and have been protesting their own country for quite some time now so it is understandable that they immediately began doing that upon our arrival. With a little time, and some investments into the region improving the quality of life, the Great Lakes region will be integrated into our nation easily. Until then, however, this will be a thorn in our side.

fields.text: Integrating the Great Lakes
lines: Integrating the Great Lakes

fields.text: After the Osean War ended in 1910, the territory that we had managed to protect was turned into a new administrative region, the Great Lakes. This continued until the reform turning former Regions into Commonwealths, when it was the backbone of the Eastern Commonwealth. The six Commonwealths form the middlemen between the leadership of our country and the people, and are a crucial part of the representation of citizens across the nation. While not ready to be added into the Eastern Commonwealth yet, pledging our goal to be to have them added to it will be a good motivator for the people to cooperate with us in restoring their livelihood. As a mere occupied territory right now, the citizens of the area do not have the same civil liberties as Osean citizens. Rather than ignoring this, showing that we seek to have them represented in our nation should please them and make them more receptive to our rule.

fields.text: A New Threat
lines: A New Threat

fields.text: News has just reached us that the head of the militarist wing of Belka's ruling party, Waldemarr Rald, has seized control of the government through a coup, and now has effective control of the country and most importantly - it's military. It seems that his predecessor's attempts to revive the economy by downsizing the military had upset Rald and his faction, whom wanted to keep the military strong. This makes our situation all the more precarious, given our recent actions towards Belka it is possible that Rald may try to reclaim the territory sold to us, likely with force. President Mackenzie has already called up the top brass of the Osean military as well as several of his advisors on how to prepare for a potential Belkan attack. Though they do not seem interested in us yet, and are more concerned with solidifying their position, there is no telling what Rald has planned for the future of his nation.

fields.text: Threatening Maneuvers
lines: Threatening Maneuvers

fields.text: Coinciding with the recent discovery of natural resources in Ustio, a number of urgent reports have been brought to our attention of the Belkan military conducting nationwide exercises and war games throughout their country. This is more than a simple routine, as their training and preparation seems to be around the clock, as well as in many types of terrain, most notably mountains, forests, and deserts, common elements on their borders with other nations. Additionally, we are beginning to see Belkan borders become tighter and more heavily militarized, far beyond a mere garrison. All these factors point to clear preparation for an invasion of one or all of their neighbors, likely in a bid to reclaim their land. While we have not disclosed this information to the public, President Mackenzie and our military command has already prepared a defensive operation for a possible Belkan attack, as well as we are reaching out diplomatically to Belka's neighbors in attempts to both warn and secure mutual alliances with them.

fields.text: Urgent War Committee Formed
lines: Urgent War Committee Formed

fields.text: Responding to the recent aggression shown by Belka, President Mackenzie has created the Urgent War Committee to assist in the preparation and defence of our nation against Belka. Comprised of several members of the military, government, and other federal institutions, the Urgent War Committe will be our foremost organizational defence against Belka, both before an invasion and during. Through quick-response communication lines and emergency authority granted to several members, the UWC will allow us to adapt and respond to any new developments within a matter of hours. With any luck, the UWC will be a vital asset to us in a Belkan invasion.

fields.text: Belkan Economic Collapse Hits Army
lines: Belkan Economic Collapse Hits Army

fields.text: Following Rald's takeover and reversal of Belkan demilitarization, the economy of Belka has been deteriorating for some time now. Despite Rald's stop-gaps, it has reached a point where even the military is beginning to break down, and as a result their war effort is declining. This comes as excellent news for us, as this means our troops will have a much easier time taking on Belka's, and their military will only continue to collapse. One can only wonder though, do they not see the writing on the wall? Why have they not surrendered yet?

fields.text: The Public Grows Tired
lines: The Public Grows Tired

fields.text: Our struggle against Belka has been bogging down into a stalemate, and as our casualties go up, the public is beginning to grow weary of our war efforts. Many are comparing this war to the Osean War of 1905, in which we lost nearly a whole generation of soldiers in a fight against Belka, only to lose. Many are calling upon us to end the war before this happens, saving those who are left. Unless we break the stalemate, these people will unfortunately be right.

fields.text:
Salvation. 

There's no other word to describe the feeling. Like the world has been handed to us. Like all our dreams have magically been granted by an almighty deity, higher than any concievable god. 

Perbla have offered to assist us in our time of neeed and open a second front against the Osean Federation. Another front means relief from ours, meaning potential breakthrough, and breakthrough means victory. 

Well, we can't keep them waiting for an answer.

Perbla have declared war on us.

fields.text: Sapinish Parliamentary Elections
lines: Sapinish Parliamentary Elections

fields.text: The long-awaited Sapinish Parliamentary Elections are upon us and voters all across Sapin are flocking to the polls to cast their votes to decide the new leaders of Sapin. On the left is the Frente Republicano Unido, a coalition of liberals and socialists desiring to strengthen the power of the Sapinish legislature and make the nation more democratic. On the right is the Crown's Union, a loose coalition of monarchists, nobles, nationalists, and catholics attempting to hold onto Sapin's traditions in the face of liberalization.

fields.text: Republicans Protest Election Results!

Though the protests are currently peaceful, there's concern among the police, military, and even FRU leadership. that some more extremist elements might infiltrate these protests to start violence.

fields.text: The Ustio-Ratio Situation
lines: The Ustio-Ratio Situation

fields.text: To the north of us, a conflict is brewing between the Ratio and the nascent Ustio. The conflict is rooted in a dispute between the two nations over a chunk of Ustian land containing many ethnic Ratians, whom the Ratian govenrment believes to be oppressed by the Ustian govenrment. Ustio disputes such claims and argues that it has a right to its own territorial sovereignty.
