shipment of weapons.

fields.text: The Belka Problem
lines: The Belka Problem

fields.text:
To the northwest of us is a looming threat: Belka. The militarist nation and its ability to exert an extreme amount of hard power on the Osean continent has been an ever-present danger to us and other North Osean nations. Historically, however, the Belkans have not had a strong Osea to fight and we might finally have a chance at putting an end to the Belkan menace.

On the other hand, the Belkans have been known to pull through even at the most unexpected times and siding with the Oseans might result in our own destruction in the long-term.

fields.text: Our Friends In Oured

fields.text: The Oseans have been a strong ally of ours for ages, both thanks to aligning interests and to our mutual benefit from the amount of trade going between each others' ports. As we approach the turn of the century, many of our foreign policy establishment has been concerned about Osea's pivot towards focusing on Yuktobania and Verusa rather than the Belkans here in northern Osea. In the future, it might be the case that the Oseans will be too distracted to help us against the Belkans and we might need to consider forming our own alliance to fight a possible Belkan invasion with.

fields.text: Formation Of NOTO
lines: Formation Of NOTO

fields.text:
The [FROM.GetName] has announced the formation of the North Osean Treaty Organization (NOTO) as an independent military alliance designed for the collective security of North Osea.

This is a sharp turn away from traditional Sapinish policy, which has always been in favor of close ties between Sapin and Osea due to the nations' aligned interests and shared trade. Such a move suggests Sapin might not trust in Osea's ability to adequately protect Sapin and North Osea or possibly even Sapin's desire to be a major world player in its own right.

fields.text: Our Border Policy
lines: Our Border Policy

fields.text: Sapin is known as being a nation historically friendly to immigration and being a nation that many North Oseans desire to move to to find better opportunities. In recent years, however, more nationalist elements of Sapinish politics have created this notion that immigrants from North Osea could be secret Belkan agents trying to undermine Sapin's national security and those who aren't are stealing jobs from hardworking Sapiniards. Attempting to address this issue, the Sapinish government has tried to tighten immigration restrictions without being too restrictive. However, this has just caused pro-immigration activists to be upset with the Sapinish government without fully placating the other side. As the head of the country, [ROOT.GetLeader] can make a royal decree addressing this issue.

fields.text: South Belkan Cities Demilitarize
lines: South Belkan Cities Demilitarize

fields.text: Following a continued lack of success in our military campaign, and growing weary of the constant bombings, casualties, and state of war, almost all major cities and townships in South Belka have agreed to surrender and demilitarize, refusing to host soldiers or produce war-related products. Unable to reinforce in these cities, we have been forced to retreat, begrudgingly allowing the Osean Army to move through these territories unimpeded. While not shattering, this is a major setback and represents a large portion of our country effectively taken over by the enemy, which we will now have to reclaim. We have already prepared defensive positions in the north and are drafting new battle plans, even some rather extreme ones. Despite this precedent, and the now-constant stream of defections to this rebel state, the fight is not over yet.

fields.text: Betrayal Of Southern Belka
lines: Betrayal Of Southern Belka

fields.text: We were warned that it would come to this. Our fatherland in her most perilous hour has been met with deceit and by members of our own People no less. When we embarked upon this crusade to liberate our stolen lands, never did we think that victory would be snatched away with such duplicity. The South lands have always been less than fully Belkan, yet we had dismissed certain comrades as being paranoid and radical for pointing out what is now obvious: that South Belka was the weak link in our national chain. Our shortsightedness and timidity has doomed the Fatherland. Now Osea and her dogs are barking at the gates and our cities burn because of our foolish mistake in letting those mixed breeds fester in their treason and cowardice. The Holy Land of our forefathers must be protected, even if it means that our supposed brethren burn, even if it means releasing the power of Seven Suns upon our soil. The price must be paid.

fields.text: Offer from Ratio
lines: Offer from Ratio

fields.text: Following our recent acquisition of territory from Belka, our eastern neighbor of Ratio has approached us with a deal. The lands of Tyrann and Boikos are primarily Ratian in culture, as they were relatively recently conquered from them by Belka. Even after falling under our control in the Belkan Federal Law Review of 1988, Ratio has never renounced their claim on the lands, however they appear to be far friendlier to us than Belka. They have offered a deal to purchase the lands back from us for a generous price, far exceeding the actual value of the territories. This, combined with several clauses allowing us to move Ustian assets out of the land and into our core areas, and a parnership with our nation for future cooperations. This deal appears to be extremely beneficial for us, as in addition to the obvious monetary benefits, we have had extensive trouble dealing with partisan forces in the area, and as a relatively new nation in the world, the presence of another ally would be greatly valued. The only protest against this deal has come from Franek Dolas, who argues that we have spent extensive resources on the lands, and even if it was under Belkan leadership, many Ustians fought and died to conquer the land. As he argues, the strongest nation will be the one who succeeds, first it was Belka, and when they were proven weak, we rose to that position instead, and if Ratio thinks they should have the land they will need to prove their strength over us to obtain it. Aside from his ramblings, the advisory board is unanimous that this deal should be taken.

fields.text: Osea Offers Western Land
lines: Osea Offers Western Land

fields.text: We received an interesting transmission from our allies in Osea today, offering us control over our former territories that were not liberated from Belka even after the 1988 Belkan Federal Law Review. It is strange to recieve this offer from a country that does not currently own these territories, however the Oseans revealed that as a part of a trade deal with Belka, the Belkans agreed to withdraw from all other occupied territories and sell the Great Lakes territories to Osea. While we would expect Osea to take these territories and sell them to us, they have not asked for a payment or even claimed the land, and are seemingly just giving it to us for free. The only request they made was to reaffirm our friendship, which we were more than happy to do, although this does make us wonder...

This is an unprecedented move and both widens our possibilities and responsibilities greatly. For now, however, Ustians both at home and in these new territories are rejoicing for the union with their brothers, and so soon after our own liberation to. Best of all is that not a single drop of blood was spilled for this. Perhaps when all this is over we can even maintain relations with Belka, as clearly if they are dealing with Osea, perhaps they will deal with us too.

fields.text: Belkan Mobilization Along Entire Border
lines: Belkan Mobilization Along Entire Border

fields.text:
Recent intelligence assessments indicate a significant escalation of military activity along the ENTIRE borders of the Belkan Federation. This development comes amidst a backdrop of heightened regional tensions and follows a substantial military buildup observed in Belka over the past two years.

Belkan authorities have initiated a comprehensive mobilization campaign, deploying military forces and fortifying defensive positions along the entirety of the nation's border. Satellite imagery and reconnaissance reports confirm a significant increase in troop movements, equipment deployments, and construction activities along key strategic sectors of the border. However, analysis suggests that this mobilization is not purely defensive in nature; rather, it bears the hallmarks of an offensive posture.

fields.text: Ratio's Response
lines: Ratio's Response

fields.text:
In a great surprise to us, Ratio has pledged to provide vital assistance and help us in our war against Belka however possible, without directly getting involved. They justify their decision with sentiments of unity and cooperation that we shown during territorial issues from 1991, and how the peaceful entire land transition was.

As part of its commitment to support our defence efforts, Ratio has authorized the dispatch of volunteer forces to bolster the ranks of our military, providing additional manpower and expertise to strengthen the front lines. In addition, they also agreed to supply us with much-needed weaponry and military equipment, ensuring that we will have the necessary resources to effectively defend sovereignty and territorial integrity.

Furthermore, Ratio has generously offered to allow us access to a portion of its industrial infrastructure for war production purposes, providing our army with a crucial lifeline to sustain its military efforts in the face of logistical challenges and resource constraints.

We will repay this unprecedented gesture – they have our ward.

fields.text: Yuktobanian Proposition Of Referendum
lines: Yuktobanian Proposition Of Referendum

fields.text:
The proposal, delivered through diplomatic channels to both Ustio and Ratio, outlines a comprehensive plan for conducting a referendum within the disputed regions. Under the proposed referendum, residents of the affected territories would be given the opportunity to democratically determine their own fate, choosing between remaining within their current nation or joining the neighboring state.

Yuktobanian officials cite the principles of self-determination and democratic governance as the driving forces behind the referendum proposal, emphasizing the importance of respecting the will of the affected populations in resolving territorial disputes. The proposal also includes provisions for international oversight to ensure the fairness and transparency of the referendum process, with neutral observers tasked with monitoring the proceedings to uphold the integrity of the vote.

The announcement of Yuktobania's referendum proposal has sparked a flurry of reactions from both Ustio and Ratio, with government officials, politicians, and citizens alike expressing a mix of cautious optimism, skepticism, and concern. While some view the proposal as a promising opportunity to peacefully resolve the border disputes and strengthen regional cooperation, others remain wary of the potential implications of diffrent outcomes of this event.

fields.text: Belka Declines To Get Involved
lines: Belka Declines To Get Involved

fields.text:
In a decisive statement from the corridors of Belkan diplomacy, the nation has firmly declared its disinterest in intervening to mediate the border issues between Ustio and Ratio. Despite mounting international pressure and calls for regional cooperation, Belka has asserted its stance of non-interference, citing its own internal challenges as reasons for abstaining from involvement in external affairs.

The announcement, delivered by Belkan officials through diplomatic channels, underscores the nation's commitment to prioritizing its own strategic interests amidst a backdrop of economic crisis and political instability. Belkan representatives emphasize the need for the nation to focus its resources and energies on addressing pressing domestic issues, rather than becoming entangled in the complexities of external conflicts.

fields.text: A Feeling Forgot
lines: A Feeling Forgot

fields.text:
Decades upon decades have passed without the power to lift even a finger to feed our families. Since an era long before now, our nation, our people, and our home have been subject to foreign oppression, foreign rule, from a foreign land, with our needs neglected. For a time beyond generational memory, Ustian language has been forbidden, Ustian culture has been suppressed, and Ustian families have been displaced. 

Silence upon the mountain tops. 

Call it luck, call it divine intervention, call it whatever one may. But by the grace of god, our souls, and this land, our mountians once more prevail as great fortresses of freedom. Our people sing and laugh free from the boulders of burdens they shouldered a year ago. The Belkan menace has left, and we are able to make our own decisions, be our own masters. 

The future of our nation is held now in our hands. We pull the rigging of our country and let our standard fly as we sail towards a new milenia. With one decade to go, let us make it a prosperous one, and we can look beyond decades, centuries, as long as the sun and moon last, to keep our new Ustio free from foreign tyrany.

fields.text: What is History?
lines: What is History?

fields.text:
Let the Belkan recount the tale of the glorious knights around the table, as they charaded and ventured across Waldreich and cleansed the land of evil. Let the Osean speak of the times of trade, when commerce and kings came together over capital, sharing prosperity with one another. Let the Erusean speak of struggle, as they bludgon nad bleed their path across time. Let the Yuktobanian speak of strife, as man and monarch clash for control over who gets to eat and who will freeze. 

But timeless turbulance has left us without a mouth to tell our tale. To tell the tale of our states of old, of our myths and manners, of our folklore and facts across the ages. We had no hand to write the stories of the highlanders and their accounts. We had no limbs to move or dance to our songs of the great dukes of yesterday. 

Let it be that with our newfound seat of power, as well as great help from collectors and popular storage, we can ensure that we give return to our culture its mouth, hands, and limbs again. Let us reclaim what was stolen from us, centuries ago.

tale of our states of old, of our myths and manners, of our folklore and facts
across the ages. We had no hand to write the stories of the highlanders and
their accounts. We had no limbs to move or dance to our songs of the great
dukes of yesterday.
Let it be that with our newfound seat of power, as well as great help from
collectors and popular storage, we can ensure that we give return to our culture
its mouth, hands, and limbs again. Let us reclaim what was stolen from us,
centuries ago.

fields.text:
Across inns, pubs, housing and hotels, all eyes were glued on one form of screen or another, all relayed the same information, and all holding their breath. 

After decades without a voice, the Ustian people finally got their voice. And they were about to be bombarded with placation, promises, and preaching from the candidates that they would eventually choose. 

What did it feel like, to have power finally? Many felt strong, many were scared, and many were just happy that they no longer had to rely on a whim in Dinsmarck to live. But how that power would be used, and the path it would guide the nation down, would be seen in the days to come.

fields.text:
The father of the nation slouched back in his refined chair. To the outside public, he could only ever be seen with a straight back, a stern yet strong and warm smile, as well an aura of complete trust and motivation. 

Clocks keep ticking in the corner of his room. How long had it been since his greatest work? Felt like a second and an eternity at the same time. And how long would he remain in this chair? One term? Two? Several? Would he even die in it? 

All that there is to focus on anyways, is the now. Whilst he does stay, he will ensure that every man woman and child that he can ensure the welfare of, will remain smiling for the future, unlike the times long gone. But... 

God was it so tiring.

fields.text:
This was not at all according to the plan... 

It was meant to go like this: 
The population of Ustio votes Morkawiecki in, he gives them the deregulation they want, fufills his promises, earns the trust of the people, and everyone lives free and happily ever after. 

He did not realise just how extensively popular the social safety nets the father had set up really were. God, even proposing to get rid of one in government was a hassle to convince his own party, let alone the opposition. But he would do it. 

So he rose before he spoke and cleared his throat. A carefully prepared speech thought out, addressing the state of the republic and the path forwards. A statement endorsing liberty, capital, freedom. A statement endorsing the right of a free man to persue the happiness he wishes without being held back by any form of tyranny, malicious or benevolent. It was a clear jab at the ideals of the previous administration, and a complete gamble. But to mark a new administration and to create the Ustio that Kuba has conceptualised, especially after everyone has burnt hearts into the father, a drastic shake-up is required.

fields.text: The Belkan War
lines: The Belkan War

fields.text:
War has broken out on the Osean continent between the Belkan Federation and the Osean Federation. Though the Oseans are out primary geopolitical rival, the Belkans are no angels either. They are, objectively, more diametrically opposed to us politically after all.

If we do not intervene, it would, at best for us, result in both Dinsmark and Oured bloodying their noses while we grow our strength. At worst for us, the Belkans win a decisive victory and we have a new geostrategic rival to deal with. One far more militarist and nationalistic than even the most hawkish Osean.

If we intervene, it will result in Yuktobania boots on the ground and pilots in the air in Osea. It will cost us a lot of resources but could result in a strong showing of Yuktobanian military prowess along with lowering the chance of a Belkan victory. However, if the Oseans lose anyway, it would be a great embarassment for us and we will have to deal with a strong Belka.
